content:
We have a task: identify the compound from experimental data. We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (intensity 100) and isotopic pattern suggests molecular ion M+ at 193.1103. The formula we derived from isomers list: C11H15NO2 (exact mass? Let's compute: C11=132.0, H15=15.117, N=14.003, O2=31.998 => total 193.118? Let's compute precisely: atomic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, N 14.003074, O 15.994915. So C11 = 132.000, H15 = 15.117375, N = 14.003074, O2 = 31.98983 => sum = 193.110279. Yes matches observed 193.11027872702. So formula C11H15NO2.

We have carbon NMR experimental: Deltas: 166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 130.07, 130.07, 127.80, 127.80, 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23.

We need to propose SMILES that matches formula and NMR.

We have many candidate isomers from list. Need to match carbon shifts.

Interpretation: 166.4 likely carbonyl carbon (C=O) of amide or ester. 144.78 aromatic carbon attached to hetero? 132,130,130,127.8,127.8 are aromatic carbons (six aromatic). So aromatic ring present. 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23 are aliphatic carbons.

Thus likely an amide attached to phenyl (benzamide) with some alkyl substituents.

C11H15NO2: Could be N-ethyl benzamide? Let's see: benzamide C7H7NO (C7H7NO) plus ethyl group (C2H5) gives C9H12NO? Not enough. Need C11. Maybe phenylacetic acid amide? Phenylacetic acid (C8H8O2) + methylamine (CH3NH2) gives C9H11NO2. Not.

Consider N,N-dimethylbenzamide (DMF analog) C9H9NO? Not.

Our formula includes 2 oxygens, likely one carbonyl (C=O) and one ether or alcohol.

Possibility: ethyl 2-aminobenzoyl? Actually C11H15NO2 could be ethyl 2-aminobenzoate (anthranilic acid ethyl ester). That would have aromatic ring, carbonyl (ester) at 166 ppm, aromatic carbons, plus ethoxy (CH2CH3) giving O-CH2 at ~60 ppm (52.24 maybe O-CH2), CH3 at ~14 ppm but we have 19.23 (maybe CH3 attached to carbonyl? Actually carbonyl carbon of ester is 166, O-CH2 ~60, O-CH3 ~55. But we have 52.24 and 49.55 and 43.55. Could be O-CH2 (52), N-CH2 (49), and a tertiary carbon (43). 19.23 likely methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl). So maybe an amide with isopropyl? Let's think.

Structure: COC(=O)C(C)C1=C(N=CC=C1)C (one candidate). That is ethyl ester of isopropyl? Actually SMILES: CCOC(=O)C(C)C1=C(N=CC=C1)C. This is ethyl 2-methyl-? Wait: It's ethyl 2-methyl-? Contains aromatic heterocycle (pyridine). Not phenyl.

Our carbon NMR experimental: 166.4 carbonyl, aromatic carbons 144.78 (maybe ipso attached to hetero), 132,130,130,127.8,127.8 (six aromatic). So aromatic ring is monosubstituted? For phenyl, we expect 6 aromatic carbons: one ipso attached to carbonyl (around 135-140), others 128-130. So matches.

Aliphatic: 52.24 could be O-CH2 of ethoxy (CH2 attached to O). 49.55 maybe CH2 attached to N (N-CH2). 43.55 maybe carbon attached to carbonyl (C attached to carbonyl, maybe CH). 19.23 is methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl methyl). So structure could be N-ethyl-2-phenylacetamide? Let's compute: phenylacetyl amide with ethyl on N: C6H5-CO-CH2-? Wait formula: phenylacetamide is C8H9NO (C6H5-CO-CH2-NH2) = C8H9NO? Actually phenylacetamide: C6H5-CO-CH2-NH2 => C8H9NO? plus O? That's C8H9NO? Wait includes carbonyl O, so formula C8H9NO? plus O? Actually carbonyl O is O, so C8H9NO? Let's compute: C8 H9 N O? That's C8H9NO? Not match.

Our formula C11H15NO2 suggests an ethyl group (C2H5) plus maybe a methyl (C1H3) plus phenyl (C6H5) plus carbonyl carbon (C1) plus maybe O? Let's count: phenyl C6H5, carbonyl carbon C1, carbonyl O1, other O1 (ether), N1, plus side chain: maybe ethoxy (C2H5O) attached to carbonyl (ester) gives C2H5 O, plus maybe methyl attached to carbonyl (acetate) gives C1H3. Total C6+1+2+1 =10? Wait need 11. Let's compute: phenyl (C6H5), carbonyl carbon (C1), ethoxy (C2H5) adds C2, methyl (C1) adds C1 => total C10? Actually carbonyl carbon already counted as part of carbonyl group; the carbonyl carbon is part of the carbonyl carbon attached to O and aromatic? In an ester, carbonyl carbon attached to phenyl? For ethyl benzoate: C6H5-CO-O-CH2CH3 => formula C9H10O2? Wait C6H5 (C6H5) + CO (C1O1) + OCH2CH3 (C2H5O) => total C9? Actually C6+1+2 =9, H5+5 =10, O2, N0. So C9H10O2. Not ours.

Add an amide N with methyl? For N-methyl ethyl benzoate? Not.

Our formula includes N, so maybe an amide: phenylacetanilide? Let's think of N-ethyl-2-phenylacetamide: structure: C6H5-CH2-CO-NH-CH2CH3? That would be C6H5 (C6H5) + CH2 (C1H2) + CO (C1O1) + NH (N1H1) + CH2CH3 (C2H5). Total C = 6+1+1+2 =10? Wait carbonyl carbon counted, plus maybe extra carbon? Actually CH2-CO is carbonyl carbon plus CH2. So total C: phenyl C6, CH2 (1), carbonyl C (1), ethyl (2) =10. Need 11, maybe extra methyl on nitrogen (N-CH3) making C11. So N-ethyl-N-methyl? That would be N(CH3)(CH2CH3). That adds 2 carbons (CH3 + CH2CH3) = 3 carbons? Actually N attached to CH3 (C1) and CH2CH3 (C2) total 3 carbons. Then phenyl-CH2-CO (C7) total 10? Let's compute: phenyl (C6), CH2 (C1) =7, carbonyl C (C1) =8, N-methyl (C1) =9, N-ethyl (C2) =11. Yes C11. Hydrogens: phenyl H5, CH2 H2, carbonyl none, N-methyl H3, N-ethyl H5 = total H5+2+3+5=15. N1, O2 (carbonyl O and maybe? Wait amide has carbonyl O only, not second O. But we have O2. So need another O, maybe an ether? Not.

Thus maybe it's an amide with an O-alkyl (carbamate). Carbamate: phenyl-CO-O-CH2CH3 with N? Actually carbamate: R-O-CO-NR2. That has two oxygens (one carbonyl O, one alkoxy O). So formula C11H15NO2 could be ethyl phenyl carbamate (phenyl carbamate ethyl). Structure: phenyl-O-CO-NH-CH2CH3? Wait phenyl-O-CO-NH-CH3? Let's think: Ethyl phenyl carbamate: O-CO-NH-CH2CH3 attached to phenyl O? Actually phenyl carbamate: phenyl-O-CO-NH-CH3 (methyl carbamate). That would have phenyl O (O attached to phenyl), carbonyl O, N, plus methyl on N. Count carbons: phenyl C6, carbonyl C1, N-methyl C1, O-ethyl? Not.

Our carbon NMR shows O-CH2 at 52 ppm, N-CH2 at 49 ppm, carbonyl carbon 166, aromatic carbons, and a methyl at 19 ppm (likely attached to carbonyl as acetyl). Could be ethyl 2-aminobenzoyl? Actually ethyl 2-aminobenzoate (anthranilic acid ethyl ester) would have O-CH2CH3 (52 ppm), aromatic carbonyl (166), aromatic ring (6 carbons). The amine attached to aromatic (NH2) not N-CH2. So we wouldn't have N-CH2.

Our N-CH2 suggests N attached to alkyl chain.

Thus maybe structure: ethyl 2-(N-methyl)aminoacetophenone? Not.

Consider N-ethyl-2-phenylacetamide with O-methyl? Not.

But carbonyl at 166 typical for amide carbonyl also around 170-175. So could be amide.

N-CH2 at 49 ppm typical for N-CH2 attached to carbonyl (amide). O-CH2 at 52 typical for ethoxy of ester. So maybe a carbamate: phenyl-CO-O-CH2CH3 (ethyl phenyl carbonate) with N-methyl? Wait carbamate: R-O-CO-NR2. So carbonyl attached to O (alkoxy) and N (dialkyl). So we have O-CH2 (ethyl) and N-CH2 (maybe N-CH3? but we have N-CH2). So N attached to CH2CH3? Actually N-CH2 could be part of N-CH2-CH3 (ethyl on N). That would give N-CH2 at ~45-50 ppm, and N-CH3 at ~30 ppm (not observed). But we have only one aliphatic carbon at 43.55 maybe N-CH3? 43.55 could be N-CH3 (attached to carbonyl). 19.23 is methyl attached to carbonyl? Actually methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl) appears ~20-30 ppm. So maybe we have an acetyl methyl.

Thus maybe structure: ethyl 2-(methylamido)acetophenone? Not.

Let's compute fragments: carbonyl carbon 166, aromatic 6 carbons, O-CH2 52, N-CH2 49, carbon attached to carbonyl (maybe CH) 43.55, methyl 19.23. That accounts for 1+6+1+1+1+1 =11 carbons. Good.

So carbon attached to carbonyl (43.55) could be the carbon alpha to carbonyl (CH) in an amide: -CO-CH- . Methyl attached to carbonyl (19.23) could be -CO-CH3 (acetyl). So maybe we have an acetamide attached to aromatic: phenyl-CO-CH(CH3)-N-CH2CH3? Wait carbonyl carbon 166, then carbonyl attached to aromatic? Actually carbonyl attached to aromatic (benzoyl) gives carbonyl carbon ~200 for ketone, but amide carbonyl attached to aromatic (benzamide) ~165-170. So carbonyl carbon attached to phenyl (C=O attached to phenyl). Then alpha carbon (CH) attached to carbonyl? In benzamide there is no alpha carbon. So maybe carbonyl is part of an ester: phenyl-CO-O-CH2CH3 (ethyl benzoate). Then O-CH2 52, CH3 of ethyl would be ~14 not observed (maybe 19.23). But we have N-CH2 49 not present.

Thus maybe carbonyl attached to N (amide) and O (carbamate). So carbonyl carbon attached to phenyl (aryl) and O-ethyl and N-CH2? That's a phenyl carbamate: phenyl-O-CO-N-CH2CH3. In that case O-CH2 is 52, N-CH2 is 49, carbonyl 166, aromatic 6 carbons, methyl? There's no methyl besides ethyl CH3 (should be ~14). But we have 19.23 maybe the ethyl CH3 (shifted upfield due to O). Ethyl CH3 attached to O appears ~14-15. 19 is a bit higher maybe due to being attached to N? Actually N-CH3 appears ~30. So 19 could be ethyl CH3 attached to O.

Thus structure: phenyl-O-CO-N-CH2CH3 (ethyl phenyl carbamate). SMILES: CCOC(=O)Oc1ccccc1? Wait that's ethyl phenyl carbonate (phenyl-O-CO-O-CH2CH3) not carbamate (no N). For carbamate need N: O-CO-N. So ethyl phenyl carbamate: O=C(OC)N? Actually phenyl carbamate: O=C(OC)N? Let's write: O=C(OC)N? Not.

Our formula C11H15NO2: phenyl (C6H5) + carbonyl C (1) + O (2) + N (1) + ethyl (C2H5) = C9? Wait phenyl O-CO-N-CH2CH3: phenyl attached to O (phenoxy). So phenyl O (C6H5O). Carbonyl C (1) + carbonyl O (1) + N (1) + ethyl (C2H5). Total C =6+1+2=9? Actually carbonyl carbon is counted, ethyl adds 2, phenyl adds 6 =9. Need 11, missing 2 carbons. So maybe N-ethyl-N-methyl? That adds extra carbon (CH3) making C10? Actually N-ethyl-N-methyl adds 2 carbons (CH3 + CH2). That would give C11. So structure: phenyl-O-CO-N(Et)Me. SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Oc1ccccc1? Wait O attached to phenyl: O-CO-N(Et)Me. So SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Oc1ccccc1. Let's compute formula: phenyl O (C6H5O), carbonyl C (1), carbonyl O (1), N (1), ethyl (C2H5), methyl (C1H3). Total C =6+1+2+1=10? Wait carbonyl carbon counted, ethyl 2, methyl 1 => total C =6+1+2+1 =10. Hmm still 10. Actually we missed the carbonyl carbon? Already counted. So 6+1+2+1 =10. Need 11. Maybe phenyl attached directly to carbonyl (benzamide) not via O. So structure: N-ethyl-N-methyl benzamide: C6H5-CO-N(Et)Me. That gives phenyl (C6H5), carbonyl C (1), N-ethyl (C2), N-methyl (C1) =10. Still 10. Need extra carbon maybe a methyl on phenyl (toluamide). So maybe N-ethyl-N-methyl p-tolamide (para-methyl). That adds CH3 on ring (C1). So total C11. So SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Cc1ccccc1? Wait carbonyl attached to phenyl with methyl substituent? Actually p-tolamide: CH3-Ph-CO-N(Et)Me. SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Cc1ccccc1? But carbonyl attached to phenyl (C=O attached to phenyl). So SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Cc1ccccc1? That seems carbonyl attached to CH2? Not.

Better: CH3-Ph-CO-N(Et)Me: SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Cc1ccccc1? Wait carbonyl carbon attached to phenyl directly: Cc1ccccc1C(=O)N(C)CC. Actually phenyl with methyl substituent (CH3) at para? Simpler: Cc1ccccc1C(=O)N(C)CC. Let's compute formula: phenyl with methyl (C7H7) plus carbonyl C (1) =8, N-methyl (1) =9, N-ethyl (2) =11. Hydrogens: phenyl methyl (CH3) 3, phenyl ring hydrogens 4 (since one position substituted by carbonyl, one by methyl) =4, carbonyl none, N-methyl 3, N-ethyl 5 = total H =3+4+3+5=15. N1 O2 (carbonyl O plus maybe? Wait amide has only one O. Need O2, but we have only carbonyl O. So missing second O. So not.

Thus need two oxygens: carbonyl O and maybe an ether O elsewhere. So maybe structure is an ester with amide? That's carbamate we considered.

Carbamate N-ethyl-N-methyl phenyl carbamate: phenyl-O-CO-N(Et)Me. That has O phenoxy, carbonyl O, N, ethyl, methyl. Count carbons: phenyl (6), carbonyl C (1), ethyl (2), methyl (1) =10. Still missing one carbon. Could be phenyl has a methyl substituent (toluyl). So p-methyl phenyl carbamate: (CH3)C6H4-O-CO-N(Et)Me. That adds extra carbon, total C11. So SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Oc1ccc(C)cc1. Let's compute formula: phenyl with methyl (C7H7), O attached to phenyl (O), carbonyl C (1), carbonyl O (1), N (1), ethyl (C2H5), methyl (C1H3). Carbons: 7+1+2+1 =11. Hydrogens: phenyl methyl 3, ring hydrogens 4 (since two substituents), ethyl 5, N-methyl 3 =15. O2, N1. Good matches formula.

Now check carbon NMR: aromatic carbons: we have substituted phenyl with two substituents (O-CO-N and CH3). Expected aromatic shifts: ipso attached to O (around 155-160), ipso attached to CH3 (around 135), others around 128-130. Our observed: 144.78 (maybe ipso attached to O), 132,130,130,127.8,127.8 (others). Good.

Aliphatic: O-CH2 (ethyl) at 52.24 matches. N-CH2 at 49.55 matches. N-methyl maybe 43.55? Actually N-methyl attached to carbonyl via N, shift ~30-40. 43.55 plausible. Methyl attached to aromatic (para) at 19.23 (aryl methyl ~20). Yes matches.

Thus candidate SMILES: CCOC(=O)N(C)Oc1ccc(C)cc1

Let's validate SMILES.
